text:
pagerduty-bot: INC/PG-9310 - sudden tail latency increase on /v1/streaming (p99) -> paging oncall
oncall: taking this, posting initial checks
erin: p95 ~360ms but p99 jumped to ~2.8s starting 20:07 UTC across eu-central-1 streaming cluster. stream_chunk_gap shows many gaps >5s
frank: seeing correlated spikes in grpc_reconnects and a small uptick in upstream 5xx from serving runtime
gina: any deploys or config flips in the hour prior?
oncall: none. Autoscaler kicked once at 20:05 due to load but queues were steady. Suspect infra layer.
erin: looking at node metrics: gpu-node-21 in stream-pool shows repeated thermal-throttle events and a sequence of PCIe link retrains. NVML reports ECC single-bit increments
hw-support: grabbing BMC and sensor telemetry now. Could be fan or VRM. Past patterns show fan PWM stuck or stuck in low RPM causing thermal ramp
frank: if GPU goes into throttle, runtime might pause kernels for a reset -> streaming stall while KV cache on that accelerator is invalidated
oncall: mitigation plan: 1) cordon gpu-node-21 + drain sessions 2) failover active streams to model-compact fallback (non-GPU) for affected sessions 3) enable extended KV prewarm on targets
erin: initiating cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-21 && ./drain-stream-node --node gpu-node-21 --grace 30s`
ops-bot: drain job queued: drain-1813456789-1 started
gina: redirecting traffic rules: added weighted routing to route 18% to model-compact variant for customers with streaming SLA <= 99.5%
frank: checking dmesg and kernel logs, got repeated messages:
```
[ 5021.987654] NVRM: Xid (PCIe:0000:af:00): 62, GPU has fallen off the bus, continuing resets
[ 5021.987660] thermal_design: GPU 0 temp reached 101C, throttling clocks
NVML: ECC single-bit errors on GPU1: 42 -> 71 in 5m
```
hw-support: BMC shows fan tach drops to 0 for brief intervals and PSU VRM temp rising. Could be intermittent power rail glitch or fan controller firmware loop
erin: rerouting in progress. After initial drain/policy change p99 improved to ~540ms within 4 minutes
oncall: customer impact: 12 customers saw buffered streaming and reconnects; 1 high-profile customer experienced 5xx for ~6 minutes during reset storms
gina: CS notified top-10 impacted customers, ops flagged mitigation steps and temporary credits offered by CS where applicable
frank: opened vendor hardware ticket: SUP-90012 with logs + ECC counters + BMC dumps uploaded to s3://redwood-support/incident/1813456789/sup-90012/
hw-support: performed soft power-cycle via IPMI and reseated GPU riser remotely, node returned but ECC counters remained elevated and fan PWM still unstable
erin: decided not to return node to rotation until vendor confirms. Keeping it drained
oncall: schedule maintenance window for 03:00 UTC for on-site RMA if vendor recommends. Marking incident severity SEV2 while pages ongoing then downgraded to SEV3 after mitigations effective
frank: postmortem action items: - add alert for NVML ECC delta > 25 within 10m - add page rule for stream_chunk_gap > 2s AND p99 > 1s - automate immediate cordon on Xid 62 or 79 events - add KPI in console for streaming tail latency by model variant
ops-bot: note: handoff to next oncall in 45m; leaving runbook notes at /incidents/handovers/1813456789.md
Gina: I'll coordinate customer comms and CS follow-ups.
hw-support: vendor initial assessment points to possible fan controller MCU firmware regression causing PWM to drop under certain temperature conditions -> thermal throttle -> ECC bursts -> PCIe link retrains. Vendor asked to collect full nvml + ipmi + bmc logs for RMA validation
erin: attaching logs for report: `nvml_1813456789.tar.gz`, `bmc_1813456789.log` (s3://redwood-infra/incident/1813456789/)
frank: confidence: probable root cause = fan controller/firmware glitch leading to thermal excursions and ECC increases causing PCIe resets. Confidence = medium-high pending vendor RMA
oncall: incident downgraded to SEV3 at 20:45 UTC. Drafting incident report and timeline. Will keep thread open for 24h for follow-ups
erin: thanks team. I'll put together timeline + artifact links and a reproducible detection playbook for HW issues affecting streaming.
gina: tagging infra, hw-partner, obs for follow ups.
hw-support: scheduling physical RMA standby for gpu-node-21 for the maintenance window.
oncall: good job. Closing active mitigation; keep monitoring dashboards for 24h :thumbsup:
